messages.subject: unstable estimates
parts:
Hi, 

I am currently using INLA to run a negative binomial regression model. My dataset is large and include many variables, e.g. 2 categorical ones each with more than 10 categories and a few other continuous/binary variables. I found that the estimates in the output table produced by INLA is not quite stable from time to time. For example, the estimates for one variable is significant (0.025quant-0.975quant excludes 0) in one output table may not be significant in another one although the same model is tested. The marginal log-likelihood for the same model also differs. I wonder if anyone can give some insights of this issue. Or is there any ways that can help improve the model performance. I used to write model using JAGS and the number of thinning can be set to improve model performance --- presumably similarly is created for INLA. 

Many thanks,
Tao

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] unstable estimates
parts:
It might be that the log posterior is very flat near the mode, hence fine details of the hessian and how this is explored will/can make a difference.

 

A general strategy in these cases, is to do

 

r = inla(….)

r = inla.rerun(r)

 

which will rerun the analysis from where the previous one stopped. In my experience, this stabalize the results.

 

H
